result: {"decisions":[{"point":"D1","problem":"Which risk areas and activities embedded evaluators should prioritize given limited scope and expertise.","did":"Focused on four areas tied to the Hugging Face incident that fit Transluce's expertise in model behavior evaluation, and excluded cybersecurity controls and work duplicating others.","alternatives_named":["a comprehensive list of risks","improving cybersecurity controls on agent swarms","duplicating METR's frontier risk reports"],"stated_reason":"They are not cybersecurity experts and want to complement rather than duplicate ongoing activities.","quote":"This list is not comprehensive: it seeks to complement rather than duplicate other ongoing activities such as METR's frontier risk reports, and we also do not address the critical need to improve cybersecurity controls on agent swarms, as we are not cybersecurity experts."},{"point":"D2","problem":"How to determine whether lab monitoring of agent swarms is adequate, given that monitors may fail to flag misaligned activity.","did":"Proposed auditing existing monitors, adding evaluator-defined monitors, and running exploratory investigations even when no monitor fires.","alternatives_named":["relying only on the labs' existing monitors"],"stated_reason":"","quote":"Independently audit existing monitors and their findings and complement them with additional evaluator-defined monitors. Conduct exploratory investigations even in the absence of monitors detecting misaligned activity."},{"point":"D2","problem":"How to validate that monitors can detect, characterize and remediate monitors alone"],"stated_reason":"Unreleased models are more varied, have fewer safeguards, and may have poorly understood capabilities.","quote":"Embedded evaluators use access to unreleased model
